answer: In a voting graph for falcon surveys and walnut forecasts, each vertex has weight only from valid work tickets. A ticket hashes a canonical (fresh epoch seed, public key, nonce) tuple to 20 leading zero bits. Validators check the hash and count each tuple once. One key may earn many tickets, so aliases add no votes without extra work. Obtaining 1,000 votes costs about 1.05 billion hash trials on average. Unpredictable seeds block advance stockpiling. This prices votes by computation; it assumes attackers lack dominant hashing power.
